title: About this model
body: An interactive 3D atlas of the head and neck of an average adult Kazakh man and woman. It is a statistical composite, not a portrait of any real person.

Anatomy: 640+ structures from Z-Anatomy / BodyParts3D, warped with a smooth thin-plate deformation so that 11 standard skull measurements match published means for Kazakh skulls (Ismagulov et al., 2018; Mussabekova et al., 2022, 2024).

Face and skin: the ICT-FaceKit statistical face model (built from ~4,000 3D scans), fitted to measurements of living ethnic Kazakhs (Ai et al., 2001, n = 404; Cui et al., 1991, n = 258) and laid over the skull with published facial soft-tissue thicknesses.
Female head: female Kazakh cranial and facial means plus regional sex differences from CT studies (brow ridge, forehead, mastoid, larynx).
Every fact shown was checked against its source by an independent verification pass.
simpl: Soft-tissue thickness comes from a Buryat ultrasound sample (Veselovskaya & Balueva) as the closest available proxy; no open Kazakh data exist.
Living measurements come from Kazakhs of Xinjiang (China); skull means from Kazakhstan. The two samples differ slightly, e.g. head length by ~5 mm.
Neck and scalp follow the reference anatomy where no Kazakh data exist; neck circumference is not fitted.
Internal organs, vessels and nerves keep the shape of one reference body, scaled with the skull; small branches are schematic.
Hair, eyebrows and skin colour are not modelled; the surface is shown as a neutral cast.
Some Kazakh anatomical terms have no approved equivalent yet; about 175 terms are marked for review by a Kazakh-speaking anatomist.
The inner-ear model (cochlea, vestibule) is omitted because its licence does not permit this use.
